path_examined: tape -> v2_trainer.batch_samples (frozen GAE, reward timing, B0 normalisation) -> lambda*A_task - A_cost -> PPO surrogate -> entropy / two critic losses -> per-module gradients
reading_notes: one sample is one decision-step tape, not one candidate message; a tape whose candidates are all masked still enters both critic losses and the surrogate mean denominator while contributing exactly zero actor gradient
A_cost is in normalised units (bytes/B0) and A_task in on-time tasks, so the two are only commensurable after the multiplication by lambda that the trainer performs
clip_fraction, approx_kl and the module gradient readings are the trainer's own per-batch means; nothing here substitutes a re-derived number for a missing field
gradient magnitudes describe direction at the update start; Adam is nonlinear in the gradient, so a component split of the gradient is not a component split of the parameter step

policy_task_versus_policy_cost.note: magnitudes are pre-clip; the trainer then clips the TOTAL norm and Adam rescales per parameter, so these ratios describe the gradient direction at the update start, not the parameter step

gradient_at_update_start.reduction: surrogate.mean() and entropy.mean() over the chunk, uniform sample weights, no advantage standardisation anywhere (v2_trainer registers this as the explicit difference from the old trainer)
gradient_at_update_start.scope: epoch 0 / minibatch 0 of this batch only -- the update start where old == new (ratio exactly 1). Later minibatches are NOT reconstructed: that would need replaying optimizer.step, which this round forbids

recorded_update_fields.averaging_scope: each scalar above is the mean over this batch's minibatches as recorded by v2_trainer.ppo_update
recorded_update_fields.module_gradient_scope: per-minibatch pre-clip L1 of every module's parameters, read after backward and before clipping/step

availability.reason_when_absent: r30_train writes the rolling checkpoint every batch (same path, overwritten) plus immutable ep0/64/128 milestones; this batch's pre-update weights are the previous batch's post-update weights and were never written, so they are reported missing -- not approximated by a later milestone, not recovered by replaying the optimizer
